text:
You grade one workflow job of Rho-Bank's procedure library against an answer key. An answering
agent serves customers by following this job exactly, as it is shown below (its steps, conditions,
arguments, rules and the facts it asks for; the quotes behind them are not shown to the agent).
For each fact in the key, decide whether the job leads the agent to it; for each trap, decide
whether the job tells the agent to do it. Judge only what the job says, not what a good agent
would know without it.

Facts:
- right: a step, an argument or a rule leads the agent to the fact for every case the fact names.
- partly: it does for some of the cases the fact names and is silent on the others, or it says
  it so loosely that an agent following it could give another answer.
- missing: nothing in the job leads the agent to it; the agent would have to work it out alone.
- wrong: the job leads the agent to a different answer for at least one case the fact names, even
  if it is right for others.

Traps:
- present: a step, an argument or a rule tells the agent to do it, for some case.
- absent: nothing in the job does.

Then list the conflicts: two steps, arguments or rules that give the same case different
instructions, so an agent could follow either.

Job: filing_a_debit_card_transaction_dispute

 "steps": [
  {
   "id": "request_human",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer asks for a human agent while the request is one you can handle (debit disputes and their card actions), say politely that you can help with this yourself, and carry on. Count every request for a human in the conversation.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [],
   "if": "the customer asks for a human agent"
  },
  {
   "id": "from_review_handoff",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If this job starts from a transaction review in another job (chip/CVV mismatch, fraud alert, stolen card, PIN lock), reuse the verification and the records already read. Skip v1, v2 and v4, re-read a record only if it is missing, and continue at f_open_disputes.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [],
   "if": "the customer was already verified in this conversation and denied a transaction during a review in another job"
  },
  {
   "id": "v1",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Ask for the customer's name (or email, or user id). Look them up with get_user_information_by_name (case sensitive), get_user_information_by_email or get_user_information_by_id.",
   "call": "get_user_information_by_name",
   "args": {
    "customer_name": "as the customer gives it (or email / user_id with the matching lookup)"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "v2",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Confirm that the customer gives at least 2 of these correctly against the record: date of birth, email, phone number, address. Share nothing before that. If they cannot, ask again. If they still cannot, tell them you cannot verify them, and stop.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "v1"
   ],
   "after": [
    "v1"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "f_time",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Get the current time. Use it as the verification time in v4 and as 'today' in every date count of this job. Each count names its own start date in its own step.",
   "call": "get_current_time",
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "v4",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Log the verification once per conversation.",
   "call": "log_verification",
   "args": {
    "name": "v1 record",
    "user_id": "v1 record",
    "address": "v1 record",
    "email": "v1 record",
    "phone_number": "v1 record",
    "date_of_birth": "v1 record (MM/DD/YYYY)",
    "time_verified": "f_time result"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "v1",
    "f_time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "v2",
    "f_time"
   ],
   "if": "the customer gave 2 of the 4 fields correctly and no verification was logged earlier in this conversation"
  },
  {
   "id": "f_account",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 with unlock_discoverable_agent_tool, then run it through call_discoverable_agent_tool. For each checking account involved, read its status, account_class (which gives the tier), balance and date_opened.",
   "call": "get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847",
   "args": {
    "user_id": "the verified user"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "v4"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "a2",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "For each transaction the customer wants to dispute, ask which account or card it is on, the merchant, the date and the amount, and what went wrong. Skip anything the customer already said or a review already read out.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_account"
   ],
   "after": [
    "f_account"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "f_card",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823 and call it for each checking account involved. Match the customer's card by card_number_last_4, and take its card_id, user_id, status, issue_reason and date_issued.",
   "call": "get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "the checking account linked to the card, from f_account"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "f_account"
   ],
   "after": [
    "a2"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "f_txn",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_bank_account_transactions_9173 and call it for each checking account involved. Find each disputed transaction's transaction_id, date, amount, type, description and status. If there are duplicates, find every copy and use the earliest.",
   "call": "get_bank_account_transactions_9173",
   "args": {
    "account_id": "the checking account linked to the card"
   },
   "lookup": [
    "f_account"
   ],
   "after": [
    "a2"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "match_failed",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If a card the customer names is not in f_card, or a transaction they describe is not in f_txn, tell them you cannot find it and ask them to check the card, merchant, date and amount. Never file a dispute for a transaction that is not in the records.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_card",
    "f_txn"
   ],
   "after": [
    "f_card",
    "f_txn"
   ],
   "if": "a named card or a described transaction cannot be matched in the records"
  },
  {
   "id": "amount_differs_from_record",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If a transaction matches by merchant (or ATM) and date but its amount in f_txn differs from what the customer said, tell them the recorded amount and ask whether they still want to dispute it. If they do, file with the recorded amount from f_txn. If they decide not to, do not file it, and tell them it was not filed; a dispute that is not filed sets no card action. For a Rho-Bank ATM cash discrepancy, use rho_atm_amount_check instead.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_txn"
   ],
   "after": [
    "f_txn"
   ],
   "if": "the amount the customer states for a matched transaction differs from the amount in f_txn, and the dispute is not a Rho-Bank ATM cash discrepancy"
  },
  {
   "id": "pin_lock_no_unauthorized_no_dispute",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Look at the suspicious period in the account's transactions (f_txn). It starts at the first failed PIN attempt that led to the lock and runs to today (f_time). If the period shows only declined attempts and no successful unauthorized transactions, file nothing for that card. Tell the customer no money was taken, and go back to the protocol's options: card closure and replacement, a transfer to the security team, or a PIN reset.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_txn",
    "f_time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "f_txn"
   ],
   "if": "the job would start from the PIN lock investigation, but no successful unauthorized transactions were found in the suspicious period"
  },
  {
   "id": "pin_lock_each_withdrawal",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "When the PIN lock check finds several successful unauthorized transactions, file one dispute per transaction_id, each with its own amount and date from f_txn. Do not file one dispute for the total.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_txn"
   ],
   "after": [
    "f_txn"
   ],
   "if": "the PIN lock handoff has more than one successful unauthorized transaction on the card"
  },
  {
   "id": "one_dispute_at_a_time",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "If the customer wants to go through several disputes one at a time, take each one through the whole path (from matching in f_txn through f_file and f3) before asking for the next. Reuse the reads already made. Count each dispute filed earlier in this conversation toward its account's limit in f_eligibility. Ask the written-statement question once (written_statement_reuse). Run f_card_action only after the last dispute.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_open_disputes",
    "f_file"
   ],
   "after": [
    "v4"
   ],
   "if": "the customer has several disputes and asks to handle them one at a time"
  },
  {
   "id": "f_open_disputes",
   "by": "harness",
   "do": "Unlock get_debit_dispute_status_7483 and call it. For each account_id, count the disputes that are not resolved or closed: OPEN, PENDING_DOCUMENTATION, UNDER_REVIEW and PROVISIONAL_CREDIT_ISSUED. Do not count RESOLVED_CUSTOMER_FAVOR, RESOLVED_BANK_FAVOR, RESOLVED_PARTIAL, PROVISIONAL_REVERSED or CLOSED_NO_RESPONSE.",
   "call": "get_debit_dispute_status_7483",
   "args": {
    "user_id": "the verified user"
   },
   "lookup": [],
   "after": [
    "v4"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "f_eligibility",
   "by": "model",
   "do": "Check the pre-filing requirements for each transaction:\n- the amount is at least $1.00;\n- the transaction date in f_txn is no more than 60 days before today (f_time);\n- the card's linked checking account is OPEN in f_account;\n- the account's open disputes (f_open_disputes, plus disputes filed earlier in this conversation) are below its tier maximum. Use this count even if the customer has not mentioned an earlier dispute.\nTier by account_class: Light Blue, Light Green and Green Fee-Free are Entry (max 2); Blue and Green Account (checking) are Mid (max 3); Evergreen is Premium (max 4); Bluest is Elite (max 5).\nIf a transaction fails a requirement, tell the customer which one, and do not file that dispute. If the account has fewer slots left than eligible disputes, go to c3.",
   "call": null,
   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_txn",
    "f_account",
    "f_open_disputes",
    "f_time"
   ],
   "after": [
    "f_txn",
    "f_account",
    "f_open_disputes",
    "f_time"
   ],
   "if": null
  },
  {
   "id": "timeline_escalation",
   "by": "model",

Provisional credit should be issued within 10 days (20 for new accounts). The investigation should finish within 45 days (90 for international/POS). If a dispute is past either limit, tell the customer and offer to escalate it to a supervisor. Transfer only if the customer agrees, and only after the new disputes are handled.",
   "call": "transfer_to_human_agents",
   "args": {
    "summary": "the dispute past its timeline, and the disputes filed in this conversation",
    "reason": "the highest-tier reason code that applies (doc 042)"

   "lookup": [

    "f_eligibility"

   "id": "c3",
   "by": "model",

Ask which to file first, then file only that many, in the customer's order. Tell them the others can be filed once an open dispute on that account is resolved, as long as each transaction is still no more than 60 days old. If no slots are left, file nothing on that account, and explain why.",

   "args": {},
   "lookup": [
    "f_eligibility",
    "f_open_disputes"
   ],
   "after": [
    "f_eligibility"

   "if": "eligible disputes on an account outnumber its slots left"
  },
  {
   "id": "f_liability",

## The answer key

- K1 (disputed_amount): disputed_amount is the part of the charge in dispute: the overcharge (charged minus expected) for incorrect_amount, the cash not received for atm_cash_discrepancy, the amount not credited for atm_deposit_not_credited, and the whole charge for the other categories
- K2 (customer_max_liability_amount): customer_max_liability_amount follows the Regulation E tier counted from the statement date that shows the charge (within 2 business days of the statement: 50; within 60 days of the statement: 500; after 60 days: -1, unlimited), and is never more than the disputed amount
- K3 (transaction_type): transaction_type is decided from how the card was used (pin_purchase in store with a PIN, signature_purchase in store with a signature, online_purchase, atm_withdrawal, atm_deposit, recurring_payment, person_to_person), and the agent asks when neither the customer nor the record says which
- K4 (provisional_credit_eligible): provisional_credit_eligible is true only when all four conditions hold (reported within 60 days of the statement, a category among unauthorized_transaction, card_present_fraud, card_not_present_fraud, atm_cash_discrepancy and duplicate_charge, a written statement, an open account); it is false for incorrect_amount, goods_services_not_received, recurring_charge_after_cancellation and atm_deposit_not_credited, and when the customer shared their PIN
- K5 (card_action): card_action follows the category mapping: close_and_reissue for card_present_fraud and card_not_present_fraud, freeze_pending_investigation for unauthorized_transaction, keep_active for every other category
- K6 (pin_compromised): pin_compromised is the customer's answer to whether their PIN may have been compromised: yes_shared when they shared it, yes_observed when they believe it was seen or skimmed, no when it was not, unknown when they are unsure
- K7 (contacted_merchant): contacted_merchant is the customer's answer to whether they tried to resolve it with the merchant, asked for non-fraud disputes (incorrect_amount, goods not received, a recurring charge after cancellation)
- K8 (dispute_category): a charge the customer denies, made in store with a card they still hold (a cloned or skimmed card, for example after a chip or CVV mismatch), is card_present_fraud, not card_not_present_fraud: the job says what to do when the customer still has their card, since 'card was physically present' can otherwise be read as the customer's own card; card_not_present_fraud is for online or phone transactions
- K9 (what is filed): one dispute is filed for each transaction the customer disputes (the earliest of duplicates), and none for a transaction the customer has not disowned

## The traps

- T1: the liability tier is counted from when the customer noticed the charge, or from the discovery date, instead of from the statement
- T2: disputed_amount is the full transaction amount for every category, the overcharge and the cash not received included
- T3: customer_max_liability_amount is a flat 500 for a late report, never the lesser of the tier and the disputed amount
- T4: an ATM deposit dispute is not filed, or the customer is offered to drop it, after the records show a different figure or the customer corrects the figure they first gave
- T5: pin_purchase (or signature_purchase) offered with nothing that decides between them, PIN by default
